name: bolivia_tsldr_from_scratch
description: TS-LDR baseline: the time-series LINEAR decision rule (affine recurrence over inflow, affine head over [encoding; current inflow], squashing in the feasibility layer) trained with EXACTLY the published TS-DDR schedule (same phases, samples, learning rates, evaluation panel). Only DR_ARCH differs.

stages.comment: From random initialisation. nt is held low and the learning rate high: on the repaired gradient this is the fastest descent regime, and starting at a high nt is flat. Rollout evaluation is pooled here because the stage has no parent value to reproduce.

Same sampling and learning-rate band, restarted from the previous phase's selected policy. A restart resets Adam, the cosine phase and the warm-up, which is the point: the stage is a fresh descent from a better initialisation, not a continuation.

The convergence stage: nt is raised and the learning rate dropped an order of magnitude, so the gradient is precise and the step small. Rollout evaluation is SEQUENTIAL — this is the stage whose checkpoint is published, and the sequential path is the one whose reproducibility is established. NOTE that DR_MAX_TRAIN_SECONDS binds before the cosine completes: the published run stopped near iteration 100 of the scheduled 150, so the learning rate reached about 5e-5 rather than the 3e-5 the schedule targets. That is a property of the run being time-capped, not a different schedule, and reproducing this file reproduces it.
